clue.text: Be honest please, like 26?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a request to be told the plain truth
second meaning: 26 Across sits in the same row of the grid as 27 Across, and 27 is the setter's own pseudonym, so it is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The second half only clicks once 27 Across is solved: the setter Elgar is 'me', and 26 shares a grid row with that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To level with someone is an idiom for being frank with them, and a clue in the same grid row is literally level with the setter's entry.

clue.text: Boy sheltered by immigrants illegally raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters lifts them bottom to top, so they read backwards
something sheltered by these words lies inside them, spanning the gap between two of them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A boy is being hidden by people who entered the country unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Ellis Island was where immigrants to the United States were processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis is a male first name, so a boy in crossword terms.

clue.text: Understanding is boundless XXX

indicators.note: without bounds means without edges, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten, written here three times

explanation.surface: A hint that a romantic understanding is unlimited kisses, or perhaps something risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: XXX looks like kisses or an adult rating, but each X is the Roman numeral; trimming T and N off TENTENTEN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, so an understanding.

clue.text: My Learned Friend may be given a ticking-off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a barrister, addressed in court as my learned friend, wears a wig
second meaning: to wig someone is an old informal verb for scolding them

explanation.walkthrough: British barristers wear horsehair wigs in court and call each other 'my learned friend'. A ticking-off is a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bewigged barrister is literally wearing a wig, and someone scolded has been given a wigging.

clue.text: Reach my throne room empty? It'll want livening up!

definitions.text: Reach my throne room empty? It'll want livening up!

indicators.note: livening something up stirs it into new activity, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Arriving at a deserted throne room, the speaker thinks it needs cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Charles II took the throne after the Puritan years left it empty, and he livened things up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Monarch is the nickname of Charles II, famed for restoring fun and pleasure to court after Cromwell's austere rule.

clue.text: See 5
Maybe regular staff changes, so a learner often looks round

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word is wrapped about the others

parts.note: much, as in 'do you go there much?', means often
sic is Latin for so or thus
taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
airs are appearances or manners, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: An office where staff are frequently reshuffled, and a trainee keeps glancing about.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is the Latin word printed after a quotation to mean 'thus, as written'; airs as in 'airs and graces' are looks or manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is a party game, and the phrase is used figuratively for a frequent reshuffling of people's jobs.

clue.text: Nancy's golden service enthrals flash tea party guest?

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so one piece is held inside the others

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, so golden is put in French: d'or, of gold
a mo is a moment, as in 'in a flash'
use, as in 'of service', means being useful

explanation.surface: A posh golden tea service in Nancy holds a flashy guest at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name but is the French city, which is why golden is translated. The French pieces D'OR and USE together hold MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dormouse is one of the guests at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: A little easier to work with one's mum?

indicators.note: letters set to work are put through their paces and come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Going out to work is slightly easier when your mother comes too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little easier' reads as a phrase, but A little is the definition and easier is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in some measure means to a partial or limited degree, that is a little.

clue.text: Sombre minimum provision at Pitié-Salpêtrière?

parts.note: the smallest provision is a single one, and the setting is French, so one is un
what a patient is provided with at this Paris hospital is a bed, in French lit

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark about the bare-bones care at a famous Parisian hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitié-Salpêtrière is a large Paris hospital, so the provision is expressed in French: UN LIT, a bed, read as one English word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlit is dark, and darkness gives the gloomy, sombre quality the definition asks for.

clue.text: Apprentice divers on here, punctuating good service at sea

indicators.note: to punctuate is to break into something, so the shuffled letters are set between two other pieces
divers is an old word for various or assorted, so the letters come in a different arrangement

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written, to be rearranged
the Royal Navy is the service that operates at sea

explanation.surface: A trainee diver is being briefed on the boat before a dive with the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the underwater people, but it is the old adjective meaning sundry; the reworked letters sit inside G...RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, just as an apprentice is a novice still learning a trade.

clue.text: Hypocritical about burying past

indicators.note: burying something puts it underground, out of sight inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: in re is the Latin legal phrase meaning concerning
since as an adverb means ago or in the past

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of hypocrisy for hiding their own history.
explanation.walkthrough: In re, Latin for 'in the matter of', is used in legal and business letters to mean concerning; it splits in two to hold the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insincere means saying what you do not feel, which is the essence of being hypocritical.

clue.text: I love how radio-operator begins and signs off!

definitions.note: what the famous lover would declare

indicators.note: the start and the close of the word are the only parts kept, and both are the same letter

parts.note: the word starts and ends with the same letter, which a radio operator would call by its phonetic codeword

explanation.surface: An enthusiast admires the way a radio operator opens and closes a transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: R begins and ends radio-operator, and in the NATO phonetic alphabet R is ROMEO, the word a radio operator actually says.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal lover, so 'I love' is a playful way of describing him in his own voice.

clue.text: So-called thriller writer kind of pedestrian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Eric ..., the English author of spy thrillers
second meaning: someone who walks at a slow, leisurely pace

explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' hints that the writer's surname is also an ordinary word, which is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler wrote classic espionage novels, and anyone strolling unhurriedly on foot is an ambler.

clue.text: Lovely having river work — sadly, it will take a toll

definitions.text: sadly, it will take a toll

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so the first word takes the others into itself

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman, a lovely
R is the standard abbreviation for river
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A beautiful riverside job comes at a sad cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a toll' suggests harm, but here toll means the slow ringing of a bell, and 'sadly' hints at a funeral knell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-rope is pulled to ring a church bell, so it is what makes a bell toll.

clue.text: A cinema in a tower, once you and I exchanged

indicators.note: one thing exchanged for another means a letter is taken out and something else put in its place

parts.note: taken as written
to tower is to rise up high
thou is the archaic form of you
taken as written: the letter to be swapped out

explanation.surface: Someone describes a picture house built inside an old tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the pronoun as archaic, the form used in old Bibles and poetry; 'you and I exchanged' means the pronoun takes the place of the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An art house is a cinema that screens independent and foreign films rather than mainstream releases.

clue.text: See 19
Get in touch with Will Moon

parts.note: to call someone is to contact them
'is to' expresses a future intention, as will does: he is to go = he will go

explanation.surface: An instruction to contact a man called Will Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Will makes it look like a first name, with Moon his surname; really it is the auxiliary verb and Moon is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large Galilean satellites orbiting Jupiter, so it is a moon.

clue.text: So Elton says, 7's not his forte?

definitions.text: So Elton says, 7's not his forte?

parts.note: surface reading: a quotation from Elton John, who is known for his song titles
setter's reading: in the party game at 7 Down, whoever is left on their feet when the music stops is out, so someone poor at it would say this

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a 1983 Elton John hit; it doubles as the plea of a hopeless party-game player who never grabs a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title is literally what a loser at that game would announce, since being left upright means failing to find a seat.

clue.text: Theatrical gag goes to the Listener

indicators.note: what reaches a listener is the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating, and wees is the informal word for that

explanation.surface: A stage joke is handed over to someone in the audience, or to the Listener crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L suggests The Listener, a famously hard crossword series; here it simply means someone hearing the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang a wheeze is a comic gag or stock joke, and more generally a clever trick or scheme.

clue.text: Castle exposed King with check

indicators.note: something exposed has had its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: Charles is the name of the reigning King
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A chess position in which the castle leaves the king open to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words King, check and Castle all point to a game, but Castle is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech is a medieval fortress in north Wales built by Edward I, so a castle.

clue.text: Customs of e.g. New York Times

parts.note: New York is an example of a US state or city
ages are eras or times

explanation.surface: A reference to the traditions or style rules of the New York Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' reads as the newspaper; it splits into an example of the US and a word for eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are established practices or habitual ways of doing things, which is what customs are.

clue.text: Distracted Brass author leaves us both hanging

indicators.note: a distracted mind is all over the place, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to leave somewhere is to depart, so the named letters depart from the larger group

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: these letters go
taken as written: these letters go too

explanation.surface: A writer about brass, or of a work called Brass, distractedly walks off and leaves two people waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' seems to go with 'leaves us both hanging'; it is the definition. Removing U, S, B, O, T, H from BRASS AUTHOR leaves R, A, S, A, R to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry hung on a wall, named after the French town famous for weaving them.

clue.text: The sort of arrangement Sooty promised Soo?

definitions.text: The sort of arrangement Sooty promised Soo?

parts.note: surface reading: a deal or relationship with no obligations attached
setter's reading: Sooty and Soo are glove puppets from British children's television, so neither is worked by strings

explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a yellow bear glove puppet on long-running British children's TV, and Soo is his panda friend; glove puppets, unlike marionettes, have nothing attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-strings arrangement is a commitment-free deal, and the phrase is literally true of a pair of glove puppets.

clue.text: Ascendant Queen without a country

indicators.note: in a down entry, ascending means reading upwards, so the letters are written in reverse
without means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: regina is Latin for queen, as in the royal cipher ER
taken as written: this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A rising queen who has no country to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a country' looks like the queen's plight, but 'a' belongs to the wordplay and only country is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: Going over a superb piece of jewellery

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word for the first piece is read backwards

parts.note: a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per
A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
a ring is worn as jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone is examining a fine piece of jewellery closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' looks like the definition (as in mending), but over is the reversal signal and Going alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal phrase for going there, so repairing can mean going.

clue.text: Retiring great: golfer defying the odds, producer of fine scores

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the kept letters are read from right to left
defying the odd-numbered positions means only the even-numbered letters of the run survive

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the first word
continuing the even positions across both words, these are the first, third and fifth letters here

explanation.surface: A great golfer retires after beating long odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'great golfer' as one string gives RAGLE, which reads backwards as the composer's name, also this setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar composed the Enigma Variations, so he was a producer of fine musical scores.

clue.text: Carrying marketing designs, oil company attending posters' area?

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
logos are the emblems used in branding and marketing
someone attending is present, that is here

explanation.surface: An oil firm's marketing designs are on display in an area for billboard posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' suggests billboards, but it means people who post online; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The blogosphere is the online world of blogs, the realm where people who post content gather.
